transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Spanish authorities are reporting at least 30 people are dead after a high-speed train
collision south of Madrid, Spain.
And Pierre's Miguel Macias reports from Seville.
The collision took place minutes before 9 a.m. local time, when a high-speed train traveling
between Madrid and Seville collided with the train sitting on the tracks for unknown reasons.
More than 500 people were traveling on both trains.
As a consequence of the collision, several cars derailed and fell off an embankment.
Government authorities are pointing at a human error.
The standard signalling systems reported issues about 20 minutes before the accident.
Backup systems were in place, but failed to prevent the collision.
This comes after a recent accident in southern Spain on the same railway line, after a train
jumped the track and hit another oncoming train.
Miguel Macias, NPR News, Seville, Spain.
The Federal Reserve will conclude a two-day meeting today by deciding what to do with
its benchmark interest rate.
Most observers feel the policymakers will leave rates steady.
NPR's Scott Horsley says that's even though inflation in the U.S. has continued to rise.
The most recent cost-living report we got from the Labor Department showed prices in
September were up 3.7 percent from a year ago.
That's an even bigger annual increase than the month before.
Of course, the spike in energy prices has been a big driver of inflation.
Fed policymakers did raise interest rates the last time they met in September.
But investors are betting that with the election day just around the corner, the central bank
is going to try to keep a low profile today, hold rates steady at this meeting, and then
maybe raise rates at the next meeting in December.
NPR's Scott Horsley reporting.
President Trump will visit Chillicothe, Ohio today to campaign for Republican candidates.
That includes Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy and incumbent Senator John
Husted.
A federal grand jury in Washington, D.C., has rejected an attempt by the Justice Department
to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, and PR's Ryan Lucas has more.
NPR was in the Washington, D.C., courtroom when a federal prosecutor told a magistrate
judge that the grand jury had not concurred, in other words, had rejected a proposed indictment.
The defendant was not identified, but a person familiar with the matter tells NPR it was
an attempt to indict Cassidy Hutchinson.
The person spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to speak publicly.
Hutchinson worked as a staffer in the White House at the end of Trump's first term.
In June 2022, she provided dramatic testimony to the House committee investigating the January
6th Capitol riot.
The attempt to indict her is the latest in a surge of DOJ actions targeting perceived
critics of the president.
It's also the latest rebuke from a grand jury of the department's efforts to prosecute Trump's
foes.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
Israeli officials are completing the ballot counting process from yesterday's elections.
There's no clear winner yet.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party is contending with an opposition party for
the most parliamentary seats.
After one party is judged to have the most seats, they will need to form the next Israeli
government.
After that, the party would choose who will serve as prime minister.
Netanyahu could return to that role, or he could yield it to the opposition leader, Gadi
Eisenkot.
A U.S. intelligence agency has published a photo of a mysterious Chinese spaceplane in
orbit.
NPR's Jeff Brumfield has more.
The photo was taken in 2024 by the commercial company now known as Vantor.
It shows the underside of what looks like a small space shuttle with its cargo bay doors
open.
China has been testing the spaceplane for years and landing it at a mysterious base in the
country's western desert.
The photo appears in a report from the Defense Intelligence Agency on Space Security.
The report finds that China and Russia in particular are rapidly developing space weapons
that could jam or destroy enemy satellites.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
The Milwaukee Brewers did not sweep at the World Series last night.
The Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Milwaukee Brewers in Florida 4-3.
But Milwaukee still leads the series three games to one.
Game 5 of the World Series will be played tonight at the Tampa Bay Rays' home park
in Florida.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Spain's high-speed train collides with stationary train south of Madrid, killing at least 30
Federal Reserve concludes two-day meeting on benchmark interest rate amid rising inflation
President Trump to campaign in Chillicothe, Ohio for Vivek Ramaswamy and Senator John Husted
Federal grand jury in Washington rejects Justice Department indictment attempt against Cassidy Hutchinson
Israeli election ballot counting continues with no clear winner between Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties
U.S. intelligence agency publishes photo of mysterious Chinese spaceplane in orbit
Tampa Bay Rays beat Milwaukee Brewers 4-3, Brewers still lead World Series three games to one
